A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoboRefer research. The complete main texts and Appendices A–I, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite added benchmark material and repagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, simulation results and real-world robot experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations of the 2B and 8B SFT models on RefSpatial-Expand-Bench.

M1.justification: The dedicated depth encoder, sequential SFT/RFT training, GRPO procedure and outcome/process rewards remain unchanged. The expanded benchmark evaluates existing model variants.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds RefSpatial-Expand-Bench, extending the existing location and placement evaluation to more indoor settings, including shops and factories, and outdoor streets, parking lots and parks. Training coverage and the other benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. New Table 14 evaluates only the existing RoboRefer 2B-SFT and 8B-SFT variants, without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: The additional evaluation uses 241 location and 200 placement examples, with 235 indoor and 206 outdoor cases and specified reasoning-step distributions (Tables 12–13). No changes to the settings of retained experiments are reported.

E4.justification: New Table 14 provides indoor/outdoor and reasoning-step breakdowns for both SFT model sizes, adding limited evidence on environment and difficulty sensitivity. Existing component ablations, depth-noise tests and backbone analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: There are no changes to seed, repeated-run, uncertainty or significance-test reporting. The added benchmark results continue to report point accuracies without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 14 adds expanded-benchmark accuracies: 2B-SFT achieves 50.21% location and 48.50% placement accuracy; 8B-SFT achieves 61.00% and 60.00%, respectively, with subgroup results. Existing results are retained. These are additional benchmark results, not same-setting performance improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, reasoning-step definition, SFT objective, GRPO equations and reward definitions are retained. The benchmark extension introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning depth-aware spatial understanding, RFT-based reasoning, dataset construction and robotic applicability.

C2.justification: Interpretations of depth, SFT and RFT effects remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning ambiguous human intent and depth-to-3D mapping. The benchmark addition supplies no substantive new interpretation or qualification.

D1.justification: Dataset-generation procedures, implementation details, hyperparameters, compute descriptions and resource-access information are retained. The extension adds benchmark composition statistics but no new implementation or access instructions.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to RoboTracer, LabUtopia, Robo-Dopamine and Prune4Web within existing related-work citation groups. The substantive positioning and novelty discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short benchmark-extension paragraph and marks Cheng Chi as a corresponding author. Existing prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 12–14. The previous training-data and RGB/RGB-D ablation tables become Tables 15 and 16, and appendix tables and figures reflow across pages. Existing figure imagery is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The expanded benchmark reduces the indoor-only coverage limitation of the original RefSpatial-Bench, supplying documented indoor/outdoor and step-wise results for two SFT model sizes. This modestly strengthens empirical coverage. Its contribution is limited because the extension evaluates neither external baselines nor the RFT variant, so it adds little evidence for the central comparative and RFT claims.
